newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 30.

text.p: THE DOMINION
Plan to hire out prison labour: The Corrections Department plans to hire out prisoners to business at market rates, but will pay prisoners a maximum of $5 a day. Page 1.

Kirton sceptical of proposal for doctors to join CHE: A proposal for private doctors to join forces with Good Health Wanganui was unlikely to test Coalition policy, Associate Health Minister Neil Kirton said on Thursday, because he and Health Minister Bill English shared misgivings about it. Page 2.

Minister calls for odometer and duty fraud crackdown: A crackdown on used import odometer and duty fraud -- thought to be worth at least $800 million -- was not too little, too late, Customs Minister Neil Kirton said on Thursday. Page 2.

Agency saves millions in health subsidies: Checks on subsidy claims by health professionals have saved at least $30 milion and perhaps as much as $80 million, officials told a parliamentary select committee. Page 2.
NZ Post in bid to run Argentine post service: State-owned New Zealand Post and newly formed Infratil International have agreed to a joint venture bid to run Argentina's postal service. Page 13.
Directors get 30 percent pay increase: Trans Tsman Properties has raised total payments to non-executive directos by 30 percent to $300,000 a year. Page 13.

Scheme 'won't promote growth': The goals of the compulsory superannuation proposal were misconceived and a compulsory scheme would not promote economic growth, Business Roundtable executive director Roger Kerr said. Page 13.
THE PRESS
Licences go in gaming blitz: Two Christchurch taverns have lost their gaming licences and six taverns are under investigation in a South Island crackdown on gaming offending. Page 1.

Claims on education 'bull' -- MP: Dr Liz Gordon, a former senior lecturer in education at the University of Canterbury, said the claims by ACT education spokeswoman Donna Awatere-Huata were "bull". Page 4.
Labour deal viable, says ACT leader: A Labour-ACT coalition is possible after the next election if Labour adopts a more market-friendly approach, says ACT New Zealand co-leader Ken Shirley. Page 5.
Maori women MPs back men: New Zealand First's Maori men are working hard for Maoridom, say Maori women MPs Georgina Te Heuheu and Donna Awatere-Huata. Page 5.
Kiwi Income profit up: no Palms decision yet: Kiwi Income Property Trust is still to decide whether to buy a half share in The Palms shopping centre at Shirley. Page 12.
Radio Otago takes C93FM: Radio Otago has bought C93FM in Christchurch, just three days after a rival company was refused permission to buy it. Page 12.

Macraes cuts forecast: Instability in two walls of Round Hill pit, in Macraes Mining east Otago gold mine project, has forced the company to reduct its forecast gold production by about 5000 ounces this year. Page 12.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

$250m bill for bug kill: The cost to fix Year 2000 computer problems in New Zealand organisations is expected to exceed a quarter of a billion dollars and could go as high as $450 million, according to a survey just released by Coopers and
Lybrand.

Trans Tasman defends ceo's shackle: Trans Tasman Properties director Bill Thurston on Thursday defended at the company's annual general meeting the $500,000 restraint of trade agreement reached last June with chief executive Don Fletcher.
--Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
